request: Add several cutouts into the part to decrease its weight.

actions.relational_constraint: The cutouts must remove material from the part.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the target part/body in the CAD model. The exact number, shape, dimensions, depth, and placement of the cutouts are unspecified. The preferred implementation is three longitudinal, rounded-end through-cutouts in the central tapered lever arm, subject to structural validation and confirmation of minimum wall, edge, and end-transition clearances.
steps: Select Section S02, the tapered lever arm, as the material-removal region. This section offers the largest uninterrupted volume for weight reduction and is less geometrically constrained than the pivot clevis S01 and open hook interface S03.

Do not place cutouts in S01. Preserve both mounting lugs, the coaxial pin bores, the central clevis slot, the slot-root wall, and the rounded lug material because these features react concentrated pin-bearing loads and resist lug separation.

Do not place cutouts in S03. Preserve the concave hook seat, outer hook body, throat transition, upright terminal, and terminal top because these surfaces directly capture the mating member and carry concentrated hook load into the arm.

Use the negative-y side plane identified by face code 0008, B-rep FACE 9, as the primary sketch support. This broad planar face provides the clearest side profile of the tapered arm. Face code 0010, B-rep FACE 16, is the opposite positive-y exit face for the through-cut operation.

Create or project a longitudinal construction centerline through the tapered arm between the clevis-to-arm and arm-to-hook transition regions. Reference the visible upper and lower arm boundaries from face codes 0007 and 0009 to control the remaining structural rails, but do not select those faces as cutting faces.

Project the arm silhouette and mark exclusion zones at both ends of S02. Keep the first cutout clear of the S01 slot-root wall near x=-60.75 mm and the pin-bore load path. Keep the last cutout clear of the S03 outer hook body and the narrow neck where the arm blends into the hook.

Lay out several closed cutout profiles within the central span; use three as the initial interpretation of 'several.' Arrange them sequentially along the x direction and center them approximately on the arm's side-view neutral-axis region.

Use elongated obround or slot-shaped profiles with tangent semicircular ends rather than sharp-cornered rectangular openings. Orient each slot's major axis along the length of the lever to reduce disruption of longitudinal load flow and avoid notch-like stress concentrations.

Scale the three profiles to follow the arm taper. The cutout nearest the wider clevis side may be the largest, with the middle and hook-side cutouts progressively smaller. Maintain continuous upper and lower rails and adequate ligaments between adjacent cutouts.

Fully constrain each sketch profile using longitudinal spacing, slot length, slot width, end radii, and offsets from the projected arm boundaries. Where dimensions are not specified, drive them with named parameters so the design can be adjusted after mass-property and stress review.

Apply conservative edge-distance constraints around every profile. Preserve substantial material next to the upper tapered plane 0007 and lower tapered plane 0009, and preserve larger solid transition zones adjacent to S01 and S03 than between the central cutouts.

Perform a symmetric through-all extruded cut normal to sketch face 0008 so each profile removes material across the full y thickness and opens on opposite face 0010. A symmetric or mid-plane cut is preferred to preserve the model's nominal symmetry about y=0.

Confirm that all cut volumes intersect only the single solid body and that the operation does not break the arm into disconnected bodies, open the existing clevis slot, intersect either pin bore, or merge with the hook throat.

Apply small equal-radius fillets to the cutout perimeter edges on both side openings where manufacturing and minimum-wall limits permit. If a simple edge break is required instead, use a small symmetric chamfer on the perimeter edges of faces 0008 and 0010 without materially reducing the remaining ligaments.

Recompute the solid and verify that the through-cutouts create new internal wall faces while modifying the side-plane regions represented by face codes 0008 and 0010. Retain S02 as the owning functional section for the new lightweighting features rather than creating a separate structural section.

Evaluate updated mass and center of gravity to confirm that the cutouts decrease weight. Compare the result with the original volume of 16217.422 mm^3 and report the removed volume and percentage mass reduction for the assigned material.

Perform a structural review for tensile, compressive, bending, torsional, and local transition stresses. In particular, check the ligaments between cutouts, the remaining upper and lower rails, the clevis-to-arm transition, and the arm-to-hook transition.

If stress or deflection limits are exceeded, reduce cutout width or length, increase inter-cutout spacing, enlarge end radii, or remove the cutout nearest the more highly loaded transition while retaining the weight-reduction intent.

intention: Decrease the weight of the part.
